thread.title: Sonos (SONO) IPO: What to Expect

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Sonos (SONO) IPO: What to Expect
text:
Photo courtesy of Sonos
Premium speaker company Sonos ( SONO ) is set to go public and will be listed on the Nasdaq ( NDAQ ). The company intends to offer 13.9 million shares, priced at range of $17 to $19 each.
What interested investors should expect from Sonos and the IPO?
While the past few years haven’t been kind to newly-public hardware companies, Sonos is not exactly a new kid on the block. Founded in 2002, the Santa Barbara, Calif.-based company has long been a pioneer in the audio industry. Three years after its founding, the company became the first to release a working wireless multi-room home sound system.
It has since built a name for itself by marketing its high-end speakers to hi-fi enthusiasts, particularly those music nuts sophisticated in areas of not just the sound, but also those who value the level of detail in the initial audio recording, production process and the playback. And they want all of that sound quality within the comfort of their own home.
Beyond the growing market of audio enthusiasts (called audiophiles), there’s also a sustained migration towards smart assistants such as Amazon's ( AMZN ) Alexa voice assistant and Google's ( GOOG , GOOGL ) Home. And that market gets even more crowded when factoring last year’s arrival of Apple’s ( AAPL ) HomePod. The prevailing question is, given this growing and highly competitive industry, can Sonos carve out a sizable share of the market for itself?
For now, the company, currently on pace to generate $1 billion in revenue for the fiscal year that ends this September, doesn’t have to worry about competition. And Sonos has, in fact, embraced competition. Sonos, which doesn’t currently have a smart assistant product of its own, has built its products that are (for now) compatible with Amazon and says its speakers will become compatible with Google Home later this year.
While there’s no direct compatibility with Apple’s HomePad, Sonos says it will introduce Siri on its speakers later in 2018 via Airplay 2 — Apple’s wireless connectivity technology. What’s more, as with Apple, Sonos has built a highly loyal customer base as evidenced by the fact that some 19 million-plus Sonos devices, operating in 7 million households, have been registered by customers as of the end of March. Many are repeat purchasers as some 38% of all sales in 2017 were made to customers who already owned a Sonos product.
Meanwhile, almost two-thirds of the 7 million households have registered more than one device. And that level of loyalty has been more than just a profitable niche. In fiscal 2017 Sonos delivered $992 million in revenue, which rose 10% from $901 million in 2016. The company, which was profitable in the first half of 2017, has generated a profit of $13 million in the first six months of fiscal 2018.
Assuming Sonos is on the same trajectory for 2018, the company could be on the verge of earning a profit as early as this year, putting it in an exclusive category financially when compared to the many younger tech companies with newly-filed IPOs.
